serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: Vbrick Enterprise Video Platform (EVP) is a multi-tenant Software as a Service (SaaS) offering, operated on Amazon Web Services, that enables organizations to securely deliver live and on-demand video to organizational users, anonymous users, or both. It provides central management of video assets, user access and permissions, network delivery devices, and video publishing and distribution, and integrates with customer directory services, single sign-on, and applications such as Microsoft Teams, Webex and SharePoint.

informationResources.metadataIncludedInScope: Yes. Metadata about federal customer data (D3, and the tenant and user identifiers in D6 and D7) is in scope wherever it resides, including third-party resources that receive it. All tenant data in the US environment is treated as federal customer data.

inclusionCriteria.A: Data handling: stores, processes or transmits federal customer data or metadata about it.
inclusionCriteria.B: Impact path: could reasonably affect the confidentiality, integrity or availability of federal customer data.

dataSets.name: Customer Content
dataSets.contents: Videos, audio, images, presentations, thumbnails and live streams uploaded or produced by tenants.

dataSets.name: Derived Content
dataSets.contents: Transcripts, translations, generated titles, descriptions, tags, chapters and summaries, text-to-speech audio, and other outputs created from customer content by EVP features.

dataSets.name: Customer Metadata
dataSets.contents: Metadata about customer content and tenants: titles, descriptions, permissions, tenant configuration, entitlements, search indexes, and tenant names and identifiers.

dataSets.name: Provisioned Account Attributes
dataSets.contents: Limited user and group records provided by the customer through one-way synchronization from the customer's directory or SSO provider: user and group identifiers, display names and email addresses. Local-account credentials exist only where a customer chooses local accounts.

dataSets.name: Biometric Data
dataSets.contents: Profile pictures and facial-recognition data, present only for tenants that enable Vbrick Video IQ facial recognition.

dataSets.name: Usage, Client and Device Logs
dataSets.contents: Access logs, client experience logs and logs from customer devices such as DMEs, including user identifiers, email addresses and client IP addresses.

dataSets.name: System Security Data
dataSets.contents: Audit logs, security events, configuration, vulnerability and inventory data, keys and certificates for the EVP service. May reference tenants and users but contains no customer content.

informationFlows.dataFlowDiagramReference: System Boundary Definition EVP-DOC-01-US, Appendix C – Data Flow Diagram

flows.destinationResource: Proxy/WAF → EVP Core Nodes → MongoDB
flows.informationTypeCarried: SAML assertions, session tokens, provisioned account attributes
flows.explanation: Users authenticate through the customer's SAML identity provider over TLS. EVP does not store passwords for SSO users.

flows.flowName: Authentication and directory sync – LDAP/SCIM Connector
flows.sourceResource: Vbrick LDAP/SCIM Connector in the customer network
flows.destinationResource: Proxy/WAF → EVP Core Nodes → MongoDB
flows.informationTypeCarried: User and group records; forwarded LDAP authentication requests
flows.explanation: The connector connects outbound from the customer network over an encrypted channel, synchronizes users and groups one way, and forwards LDAP authentication to the customer directory.

flows.destinationResource: Proxy/WAF → EVP Core Nodes → MongoDB
flows.informationTypeCarried: Local-account credentials, session tokens
flows.explanation: Used only where a customer chooses local accounts.

flows.destinationResource: Elastic Load Balancers → Proxy/WAF → EVP Core Nodes → Amazon S3; MongoDB
flows.informationTypeCarried: Video and other media files, metadata
flows.explanation: Authenticated users upload and download media over HTTPS. Content is stored in tenant-specific encrypted S3 storage and may be transcoded.

flows.flowName: Media upload and download – DMEs and encoders
flows.destinationResource: Elastic Load Balancers → Proxy/WAF → EVP Core Nodes → Amazon S3; MongoDB
flows.informationTypeCarried: Video files, device registration, heartbeat and configuration, software updates, device logs
flows.explanation: Customer-owned devices authenticate with access keys and exchange media and configuration over HTTPS; device logs are sent to EVP.

flows.flowName: Media upload and download – API and integrations
flows.destinationResource: Elastic Load Balancers → Proxy/WAF → EVP Core Nodes → Amazon S3; MongoDB
flows.informationTypeCarried: Media files, metadata, API credentials
flows.explanation: Integrating applications authenticate to the public REST API and transfer content over HTTPS.

flows.sourceResource: Amazon S3 via EVP Core Nodes and CloudFront
flows.destinationResource: Viewer's browser or player
flows.informationTypeCarried: Video content, access logs
flows.explanation: Video is served from cloud storage or through US-origin CloudFront distributions. Cached content is visible only to authenticated users unless marked public.

flows.destinationResource: Proxy/WAF → EVP Core Nodes → CloudFront → viewer
flows.informationTypeCarried: Live video streams (in transit only), webcast metadata
flows.explanation: EVP authenticates viewers and routes the webcast; live content is not stored in the cloud while in progress.

flows.sourceResource: SIP-enabled conference, Microsoft Teams or Webex
flows.destinationResource: Integration endpoints → Video Conference Integration services (ECS, SQS) → Amazon S3
flows.informationTypeCarried: Conference audio and video, recording metadata
flows.explanation: Conferences are recorded live, processed and added to the tenant as video on demand.

flows.destinationResource: CloudFront (dme-logs.us) → S3 log buckets → central logging
flows.informationTypeCarried: Client and device logs including user identifiers, email addresses and client IP addresses
flows.explanation: Used for remote troubleshooting.

flows.destinationResource: Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Translate → Amazon S3
flows.informationTypeCarried: Audio tracks, transcripts and translations
flows.explanation: Optional feature; outputs are stored within the boundary; AWS does not train on customer data.

flows.destinationResource: Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic Claude) and Amazon Polly → Amazon S3
flows.informationTypeCarried: Transcripts, extracted video frames, metadata, generated text and audio
flows.explanation: Optional features; only the minimum necessary data is sent; outputs are stored within the boundary; AWS and Anthropic do not train on customer data.

flows.destinationResource: Amazon Rekognition → Amazon S3; MongoDB
flows.informationTypeCarried: Video frames, profile pictures, facial-recognition data
flows.explanation: Optional feature enabled per tenant; AWS does not train on customer data.

flows.destinationResource: Proxy/WAF → MCP Server (ECS) → EVP Core Nodes
flows.informationTypeCarried: Content and metadata the user is authorized to see
flows.explanation: Requests arrive over HTTPS; the customer selects and operates the LLM and is responsible for data sent to it.

flows.destinationResource: Mail Host → Amazon SES → tenant users
flows.informationTypeCarried: Notification content, user email addresses
flows.explanation: Outbound system-generated email.

flows.destinationResource: DR-01 (us-west-2)
flows.informationTypeCarried: Replicated content and database records
flows.explanation: S3 cross-region replication and a MongoDB replica over encrypted connections; no replication to non-US regions.

flows.destinationResource: Staging-01 (us-east-1)
flows.informationTypeCarried: Replica of the production database
flows.explanation: Used only during a validation run; data never leaves the Production account and is deleted at shutdown.

flows.destinationResource: ECR and S3 build repositories → Harness delegate in Production 01
flows.informationTypeCarried: Source code, build artifacts, container images, configuration
flows.explanation: Jenkins builds and publishes artifacts over HTTPS; deployment runs within AWS under an approved Jira change request.

flows.sourceResource: Vbrick operations and support staff (Entra ID identities)
flows.destinationResource: IAM Identity Center → AWS Console / Systems Manager Session Manager → Management VPC → hosts
flows.informationTypeCarried: Administrative sessions; administrative access to D1–D6
flows.explanation: SSO with MFA; host access is brokered by Session Manager with no direct network path from Vbrick offices.

flows.sourceResource: Production hosts, Zabbix, CloudWatch, CloudTrail, Shield
flows.destinationResource: CrowdStrike, Qualys, PagerDuty, Slack, Site24x7
flows.informationTypeCarried: Host telemetry, scan results, CloudTrail write events, alerts
flows.explanation: Carries system security data and no customer content.

flows.destinationResource: Lambda functions, EventBridge rules and Auto Scaling groups in the Production account
flows.informationTypeCarried: Scaling instructions and instance events
flows.explanation: Actions are recorded in CloudTrail in the Audit account and analyzed by CrowdStrike.

certified.name: Amazon Web Services – AWS US East/West
certified.useCase: Infrastructure provider hosting the EVP service: compute (EC2, including Elastic Load Balancing and Auto Scaling; EBS), storage (S3), networking and delivery (VPC, CloudFront), containers (ECS, ECR), serverless (Lambda), messaging (SQS), email (SES), keys and secrets (KMS, Secrets Manager), identity and governance (IAM, IAM Identity Center, Organizations), logging and monitoring (CloudTrail, CloudWatch, Athena, Config, Inspector, Systems Manager, Macie), and the optional AI features (Transcribe, Translate, Polly, Bedrock with Anthropic Claude, Rekognition).
certified.usageAndConfiguration: Services used only in us-east-1 (primary) and us-west-2 (disaster recovery) within the Production account, with the Organizations management account and the Audit account.
certified.mitigationMeasures: Data at rest encrypted with AWS KMS; AI services configured so that AWS and Anthropic do not train on customer data.
certified.compensatingControls: Tracked in the Vendor Supply Chain Risk Management Tracker and reviewed monthly; vendor SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or equivalent reports and agreements reviewed annually.

certified.name: Slack
certified.usageAndConfiguration: Operations channel for change-event alerts and FedRAMP message alerts. FedRAMP Certified (Rev5, Agency path, Class C) on the Enterprise Grid plan.
certified.mitigationMeasures: Receives notifications only; no access to production.
certified.compensatingControls: Tracked in the Vendor Supply Chain Risk Management Tracker and reviewed monthly; vendor SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or equivalent reports and agreements reviewed annually.

certified.name: Paramify Cloud
certified.usageAndConfiguration: Holds the SDR, solution capabilities and Trust Center. FedRAMP Certified (20x, Program path, Class C).
certified.mitigationMeasures: No connection to production; holds system documentation, not customer data.
certified.compensatingControls: Tracked in the Vendor Supply Chain Risk Management Tracker and reviewed monthly; vendor SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or equivalent reports and agreements reviewed annually.

nonCertified.name: CrowdStrike Falcon
nonCertified.useCase: Endpoint detection and response, vulnerability management, container image scanning, CSPM and DSPM.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Falcon sensor on every production host; container image scanning; CSPM of the Production account; DSPM scanners in a dedicated VPC in the account; receives CloudTrail write events for indicator-of-attack analysis.
nonCertified.justificationForUse: Endpoint protection, vulnerability detection and configuration monitoring.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Integration roles limited to what each module needs; console access requires MFA; DSPM returns classification findings, not content.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Tracked in the Vendor Supply Chain Risk Management Tracker and reviewed monthly; vendor SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or equivalent reports and agreements reviewed annually.

nonCertified.name: Microsoft Entra ID
nonCertified.useCase: Workforce identity source for administrative access.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Groups provisioned to IAM Identity Center by SCIM.
nonCertified.justificationForUse: Central workforce identity with MFA for privileged access.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: MFA for every production access holder; Conditional Access blocks the AWS applications on devices that are not company-owned; production access through Identity Center permission sets and time-boxed approval.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Tracked in the Vendor Supply Chain Risk Management Tracker and reviewed monthly; vendor SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or equivalent reports and agreements reviewed annually.

nonCertified.name: GitHub Enterprise Cloud
nonCertified.useCase: Source control for software and infrastructure code deployed to production.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Source code, infrastructure-as-code templates and environment configuration; sign-in through Entra SSO; access by team. No access to the production environment.
nonCertified.justificationForUse: Version control for software and infrastructure code.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Signed commits verified by GitHub; pull request with one approval required on the production branch; team access reviewed at least monthly.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Tracked in the Vendor Supply Chain Risk Management Tracker and reviewed monthly; vendor SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or equivalent reports and agreements reviewed annually.

nonCertified.name: Atlassian Jira
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: The only system that authorizes work in production, including changes, access requests and log deletion; support escalations may reference tenants.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Production work is performed only against an approved Jira ticket; tickets reference tenants by name or identifier, not customer content; access limited to Vbrick personnel through SSO.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Tracked in the Vendor Supply Chain Risk Management Tracker and reviewed monthly; vendor SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or equivalent reports and agreements reviewed annually.

nonCertified.name: Salesforce
nonCertified.useCase: Customer support cases and customer maintenance notifications.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Support cases may include tenant names or identifiers; Marketing Cloud Account Engagement sends customer maintenance notifications.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: No access to production; requests in Salesforce do not drive production work unless a Jira ticket is approved.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Tracked in the Vendor Supply Chain Risk Management Tracker and reviewed monthly; vendor SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or equivalent reports and agreements reviewed annually.

nonCertified.name: Qualys Policy Audit
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Checks EC2 images and MongoDB databases against CIS Benchmarks.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Scanning credentials limited to audit functions; results reviewed by Information Security.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Tracked in the Vendor Supply Chain Risk Management Tracker and reviewed monthly; vendor SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or equivalent reports and agreements reviewed annually.

nonCertified.name: PagerDuty
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Escalates alerts from Zabbix, Site24x7, CloudWatch, CloudTrail change events and Shield.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Receives notifications only; no access to production.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Tracked in the Vendor Supply Chain Risk Management Tracker and reviewed monthly; vendor SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or equivalent reports and agreements reviewed annually.

nonCertified.name: Site24x7
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Probes public endpoints only; no credentials or access to production.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Tracked in the Vendor Supply Chain Risk Management Tracker and reviewed monthly; vendor SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or equivalent reports and agreements reviewed annually.

nonCertified.name: Cobalt
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Annual penetration test of the EVP service using a dedicated test tenant.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Testers have no access to customer tenants; credentials limited to the test tenant and test period.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Tracked in the Vendor Supply Chain Risk Management Tracker and reviewed monthly; vendor SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or equivalent reports and agreements reviewed annually.

nonCertified.name: nOps Compute Copilot
nonCertified.useCase: Compute cost optimization for autoscaled capacity.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Manages selected Auto Scaling groups in the Production account through Lambda functions, EventBridge rules and IAM roles that nOps deploys and maintains through a cross-account role; a separate read-only role supports cost analysis.
nonCertified.justificationForUse: Compute cost optimization for autoscaled capacity.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Actions by nOps roles are recorded in CloudTrail in the Audit account and analyzed by CrowdStrike; IAM changes raise immediate Shield alerts.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Tracked in the Vendor Supply Chain Risk Management Tracker and reviewed monthly; vendor SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or equivalent reports and agreements reviewed annually.

nonCertified.name: Harness
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: SaaS that orchestrates production deployment pipelines; a delegate in Production 01 connects outbound to Harness over HTTPS and runs pipeline steps with its host's IAM role.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Production deployments run only under an approved Jira change request; the delegate makes outbound connections only; delegate actions are recorded in CloudTrail in the Audit account; deployment credentials are held in AWS Secrets Manager.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Tracked in the Vendor Supply Chain Risk Management Tracker and reviewed monthly; vendor SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 or equivalent reports and agreements reviewed annually.

cryptographicModules.summary: Data at rest in Amazon EBS (including MongoDB and Elasticsearch volumes), Amazon S3, backups and snapshots, AWS Secrets Manager and Amazon CloudWatch Logs is encrypted with AES-256 using keys held in AWS Key Management Service (CMVP #4884). Connections from users and customer systems terminate at load balancers that use a FIPS TLS policy accepting TLS 1.3 and 1.2, provided by AWS-LC (CMVP #4631); unencrypted connections are not accepted. EVP hosts run Amazon Linux 2023 in FIPS mode, using the validated kernel cryptographic API (CMVP #5369) and OpenSSL FIPS provider (CMVP #5438) for operating system and application-layer cryptography. Within the production VPCs, all production instances use supported Nitro-based instance types, which use the offload capabilities of the underlying Nitro System hardware to encrypt in-transit traffic between instances automatically. Multi-factor authentication uses third-party authenticator applications, listed below with their validation status. Agency tenants use these modules by default. Modules by service are listed in the Cryptographic Modules Table (SSP Appendix Q, Version 1.4, 09 Nov 2026).

modules.servicesCovered: Data at rest: Amazon EBS (full disk, including MongoDB and Elasticsearch volumes), Amazon S3 (SSE-KMS), backups and snapshots, AWS Secrets Manager and Amazon CloudWatch Logs
Data in transit: user and customer connections from the internet to the Elastic Load Balancing FIPS TLS policy (TLS 1.3/1.2)
EVP hosts (Amazon Linux 2023): host operating system kernel
